newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seen facing meat shortages.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seen facing meat shortages.

text.p: Bulgaria's meat-processing association said on Thursday it expects pork shortages later in the season because of unprecedented slaughter of pigs in the wake of this year's poor grain harvest.
"Bulgaria soon will have to import pork. Demand for this product rises during the winter and its supplies will fall," the association's chairman Ruman Kuzmanov told a news conference.
Farmers are currently selling animals at below cost.
Bulgaria's agriculture ministry decided last week to reduce pig and poultry numbers in order to ensure fodder for winter feeding of cattle.
Kuzmanov urged the government to reduce obstacles to pork imports, which are currently burdened by a heavy import tax of $800 per tonne.
Bulgaria faces a severe grain shortage because of excessive exports last year and a poor harvest this season. It intends to import large quantities of grain and fodder.
